original_question: Does an analogue of Dunwoody’s theorem hold for totally disconnected locally compact groups, that is, must a tdlc group of rational discrete cohomological dimension at most 1 be topologically isomorphic to the fundamental group of a graph of profinite groups?
target_in_paper: The draft matches Question F* in the Introduction of arXiv:2201.10847v3 (the broad Dunwoody-type open problem for t.d.l.c. groups), not any statement in arXiv:1401.0300, which appears to be a mistaken paper ID.
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the t.d.l.c. setting, the cohomological threshold cd_Q(G) <= 1, and the intended Bass-Serre-type conclusion that G should arise as a fundamental group of profinite groups. It also correctly aims at the full Dunwoody-style analogue, rather than at the narrower results already proved in the paper under extra finiteness assumptions.
missing_details: Make the coefficient field explicit: cd_Q(G) is the rational discrete cohomological dimension, i.e. computed in the category of discrete Q[G]-modules.
Specify that the graph should be connected; in the paper the relevant object is a graph of groups based on a connected graph Λ.
Clarify what 'graph of profinite groups' means: all vertex-groups and edge-groups are profinite, and each edge map α_e: G_e -> G_{t(e)} is injective, open, and continuous.
State that π_1(G,Λ) is the Bass-Serre fundamental group equipped with its canonical t.d.l.c. topology.
Replace plain 'isomorphic' by 'topologically isomorphic'; by the paper's convention this means continuous with continuous inverse.

To stay faithful to the full Dunwoody-type question, say explicitly that no extra hypotheses such as compact generation, compact presentability, CO-boundedness, or unimodularity are being imposed; adding them would narrow the question to the proved partial analogues.
Use 'does there exist' (for a given G) or 'does every such G admit' to make the quantifier structure explicit.
refined_question: Let G be a totally disconnected locally compact group with rational discrete cohomological dimension cd_Q(G) <= 1, where cd_Q is computed in the category of discrete Q[G]-modules. Does there exist a connected graph Λ and a graph of profinite groups (𝒢,Λ)—that is, profinite vertex-groups and edge-groups together with injective open continuous edge maps—such that G is topologically isomorphic to the Bass-Serre fundamental group π_1(𝒢,Λ) equipped with its canonical t.d.l.c. topology?
justification: The supplied arXiv identifier does not match the topic of the draft. The draft instead aligns with the open Dunwoody-type question stated as Question F* in the introduction of the t.d.l.c. Stallings-Swan paper by Castellano, Marchionna, and Weigel. In that paper the authors recall Dunwoody's Theorem A, prove only narrower t.d.l.c. analogues under compact generation plus either CO-boundedness or compact presentability (Theorems B and C), and then explicitly ask the broader question whether every t.d.l.c. group with cd_Q(G) <= 1 is topologically a fundamental group of a graph of profinite groups. The nearby context also fixes the meaning of 'graph of t.d.l.c. groups', the canonical topology on π_1, and the convention on topological isomorphisms; Fact 5.5 explains why, in the compactly generated cd_Q=1 case, accessibility is equivalent to being the fundamental group of a finite graph of profinite groups, so one should not insert 'finite' unless one also narrows the hypotheses accordingly.
